commit.message: chore: update export benchmark data [skip ci]

feat(apply): the apply flow runs the staged 4-step pipeline on both surfaces (#992)

* feat(shared): let a résumé-pipeline run start from pasted text, not just ids

resumeId/jobId on ResumePipelineRunSchema get .default('') and gain
resumeText/jobAdText siblings (same 200_000-byte cap class as the
resume/job text used elsewhere), plus small-capped jobTitle/companyName/
board for the text path's posting identity. Two refinements reject a
request with neither an id nor its text on a side. The old id-only wire
shape still parses unchanged.

The exported ResumePipelineRunRequest type switches from z.infer (output,
defaults resolved to required strings) to z.input, so an existing caller
built before these five fields keeps type-checking without edits — nothing
on this transport ever calls .parse() client-side, so there is no runtime
difference to protect.

Regenerated the Rust IPC contract via `pnpm gen:ipc`.

* test(shared): cover the résumé-pipeline run schema's id-wins refinements

Old id-only shape still parses; text-only and mixed id/text combos are
accepted; either side empty on both its id and its text is rejected; the
new text-path free-text fields are capped.

* feat(resume-pipeline): resolve résumé/job-ad text with an id-wins rule

execute() now takes a nonempty resumeId/jobId (DocumentStore/postings-cache
lookup, hard error on a miss — never a silent fallback to text) OR clamped
resumeText/jobAdText, per side. sourceResumeId is written to the run's
metrics ONLY on the id path, so a text-path run's later regenerateSection
correctly falls through source_resume_for's documented weaker fallback
(and PR-1's provenance gate still refuses to write projects from it).

Also persists the text path's job-ad text into the aggregate's job_ad
column (today deliberately empty on the id path — the postings cache is
keyed by a live job id a finished run no longer holds); the id path is
unchanged and merge_application's pick() keeps any existing job_ad.

The clamp + the pure id-wins decision moved to a new resolve.rs to keep
mod.rs under R8's per-module LOC cap.

* test(resume-pipeline): cover the id-wins resolution and text-path caps

resume_source/job_source: id wins even when text is also present, falls
back to text only when the id is empty, None when both are empty/
whitespace. job_meta_from_request reads the four identity fields off the
clamped request. job_ad_for_persist is empty on the cache path and carries
the text on the text path. Two grep-shaped checks (this crate has no
AppHandle test harness) pin that the id arms never read the text fallback
and that sourceResumeId is gated on the Store path. Extends the existing
clamp test for the five new fields.

Every new assertion was mutation-checked (temporarily broken, confirmed
red, reverted).

* feat(renderer): split the letter stream and add the 4-step pipeline mapper

- usePipelineDraftStream forwards reasoning/thinking chunks to an optional
  onThinking callback (previously dropped).
- useResumePipelineSession snapshots the draft into its own letterDraft
  buffer once the cover_letter stage starts, so letter tokens stop mashing
  onto the resume pane; also exposes a thinking accumulator.
- new pure pipelineStepForStage mapper folds the 8 quality-pipeline stages
  into the 4 apply-flow steps (analyze/generate/validate/humanize).

* feat(renderer): surface which saved doc backs the resume input card's text

Optional onDocIdChange prop reports the selectedDocId already tracked
internally, and clears to null on a manual edit (the paste textarea
previously bypassed the id-tracking state entirely). Feeds the apply
flow's id-wins pipeline run request (resumeId vs resumeText).

* feat(renderer): drop the tailor wizard's depth picker, add the 4-step i18n copy

StepModel loses DepthSelector + depthUnavailableReason plumbing (the apply
flow always runs the staged quality pipeline now) and shows an honest cost
line instead. tailor-schema/tailor-state drop depth, add resumeDocId
(wired from StepResume via ResumeInputCard's new onDocIdChange).

New pipeline.step.* i18n (en+de, label+description x4) for the coming
4-step checklist; drop the now-orphaned autopilot.apply.generatingHint/
reasoningHeavyHint keys.

* feat(renderer): add the staged-run hook and the 4-step generating panel

useTailorPipeline wraps useResumePipelineSession with the page-local UI
state useTailorGeneration used to own (active doc, copy/export, inline-edit
overrides, quality re-check, section-fix/fabrication-review wiring,
id-wins run request). Resume text comes from the run detail; letter text
from the job's aggregate ai_generations record (the pipeline writes both
directly). Invalidates that aggregate once the run leaves running.

GeneratingPanel drops the fast-path phase dots for the 4-row checklist
(analyze/generate/validate/humanize) driven by the new pipeline-steps
mapper, keeping ThinkingBubble/streaming text/Cancel; dropped the
reasoning-heavy hint (superseded by the finer per-stage progress).

GenerationOutput gains an optional pipeline prop forwarded to QualityBadge
(fast-path callers unaffected — undefined by default).

TailoredResumePanel's test fixture gets the two new session fields
(letterDraft/thinking).

* feat(renderer): give the tailor results panel a staged-run status banner

Prominent (not hidden behind a click) needsReview/cancelled/error status
above the document viewer, plus this posting's read-only run history
(PipelineRunsList) below it — both new, additive to the existing
height-bounded GenerationOutput body (the scroll-boundary regression
guard still holds: nothing new sits between it and the panel body).

GenerationOutput now receives the section-fix / fabrication-review bundle
(pipelineReview) so the quality badge/panel wires Fix and per-bullet
Keep/Remove for a staged run.

* fix(renderer): cold-entry fallback for the tailor pipeline's resume text

resumeOut and the quality report now fall back to the job's persisted
aggregate record when no live run detail exists yet (a fresh session that
never started/reconnected a run) — the letter already worked this way;
the resume text and the report did not, which would have shown an empty
done stage on reopen even though a saved result existed.

* feat(renderer): cut the tailor flow over to the staged quality pipeline

index.tsx now runs useTailorPipeline instead of useTailorGeneration:
stage derivation keys on busy/hasOutput, GeneratingPanel gets the 4-step
checklist props, ResultsPanel gets the pipeline-review bundle + run
status + run history. The reconnect target ({runId, jobId}) persists via
a new persistence.runId/runJobId pair (session-store applyRunId/
applyRunJobId, reset alongside the other one-shot fields on switching
applications) instead of the deleted generation-store.

useTailorPipeline.start() now also toasts a failed launch (the session
itself only sets the persistent banner text) — parity with the fast
path's onError toast.

Rewrote both TailorFlow test files: the extraction-seam suite mocks the
new hook's shape; the failure-visibility suite now drives a REAL
useTailorPipeline -> useResumePipelineSession chain against a mock
AppClient (resumePipeline.run/get) instead of the deleted generation
pipeline stubs.

* chore(renderer): delete the fast-path tailor engine, dead after the cutover

store/generation-store/ and useTailorGeneration(.test).ts had exactly one
consumer — TailorFlow — confirmed by grep before deleting; ai-generate and
resume-builder call lib/generate/generation directly and keep their own
one-shot path untouched.

Drop the now-orphaned autopilot.apply.{depthUnavailable,analyzing,
writingResume,writingCover,generating} i18n keys (en+de) — only ever read
by the deleted hook/store.

* fix(renderer): reseed the resume input card's doc id across a step remount

ResumeInputCard's `selectedDocId` was component-local `useState(null)`, so
it reset on every mount while the wizard's form field (`resumeDocId`) did
not. TailorWizard renders `{step === 1 && <StepResume />}`, so navigating
away from and back to the resume step remounts the card: the form still
held the previously-selected doc id, but the card's local state forgot it.
Two handlers gate on that local id and both silently misbehaved as a
result — `handleTextChange` never told the host a hand edit had
invalidated the id (so `useTailorPipeline.start()` kept sending the stale
`resumeId`, discarding the user's edit per the backend's id-wins rule),
and `handleRemove` failed to clear the host's id when the removed doc was
the one actually backing the text.

Fixed at the root instead of patching each gated call site: `useResumeInput`
now accepts an optional host-owned `docId`, used only as the `useState`
initializer, so a remount re-seeds local state from what the host already
believes. This keeps local and host state in lockstep for every existing
call site (including the `handleRemove` sibling) without touching any of
their conditionals, and is a smaller diff than special-casing each one.
`StepResume` seeds it from `getValues('resumeDocId')`. The backend's
id-wins rule is untouched — only the renderer's provenance signal was wrong.

Tests: hook-level remount regression + happy path in
useResumeInput.test.ts, and a StepResume.test.tsx integration test with a
real react-hook-form instance shared across an unmount/remount, asserting
the form's resumeDocId field itself clears on a post-remount edit.

* fix(resume-pipeline): make id-wins resolution behavioral, not lexical

rust-backend-architect (MEDIUM 1): resume_source/job_source stayed pure,
but execute's Store/Cache arms were inline matches — a source-substring
test pinned their SPELLING, and a mutation that aliased clamped.resume_text
through a differently-named local passed it while changing the guarded
behavior. resolve_resume/resolve_job close this structurally: the id arm
receives only an id and an injected lookup closure, so there is nothing in
scope to fall back to on a miss, provably (the lookup can return None and
the function still cannot do anything but error). source_resume_id_for_
metrics gets the same treatment for the sourceResumeId metrics gate.

rust-backend-architect (MEDIUM 2): PipelineRunStore::prune partitions
retention on (job_url, kind), and every unlinked run shared job_url = ""
there — harmless while rare, but the text path makes an unlinked run
routine (a pasted job ad, an Autopilot job with no capturable link), so
every pasted posting's history pooled into one shared bucket. run_store_
job_url substitutes a stable per-text synthetic key (unlinked_run_key) for
the RUN ROW only, shaped as an https://…/.invalid url (RFC 2606) so it
survives PipelineRunStore::upsert_run's own normalize_job_url call (which
neutralizes any other scheme back to "") without ever being mistaken for a
resolvable posting link. The aggregate's own job_url (persist_document's,
what save_application upserts by) is untouched — different table, different
trust level, documented on job_ad_for_persist alongside the SEC-LOW-4 note
that the text path's aggregate key is the renderer's own unverified claim.

rust-backend-architect (LOW 1) + tauri-security-reviewer (SEC-LOW-3):
resumeId/jobId are now clamped in clamp_request (JOB_IDENTITY_CAP, 512
bytes) like every other renderer string on this command, and resolution
reads the clamped copies — closing the two unbounded echo points (a
validation-error message, metrics_json). The echoed id is additionally
capped to 64 chars for the error message specifically, mirroring
agent::tools::clamped_echo/ECHO_CAP's exact rule but reimplemented locally
rather than imported: agent::tools is PR-5's deletion target and
clamped_echo isn't part of its fenced/JOB_CAP/RESUME_CAP extraction, so
depending on it here would force PR-5 to widen scope or break this command.

Split run_store_job_url out alongside the rest of resolve.rs's pure
resolution logic to keep mod.rs under R8's LOC cap after these additions.

* fix(resume-pipeline): collapse whitespace in the notification posting label

tauri-security-reviewer (SEC-LOW-2): a jobTitle/companyName carrying an
embedded newline (scraped, or PR-3's untrusted text-path fields) survived
into the OS notification body verbatim — a one-line label becoming two —
and on a Linux desktop whose notification daemon advertises libnotify
body-markup, an embedded <b>/<a href> reads as markup rather than text.
collapse_whitespace runs before the label is assembled, subsuming the old
.trim() and closing the newline-driven multi-line case.

* test(resume-pipeline): cover the pure resolve functions and retention key

Replaces the two source-substring grep tests (id-path-never-falls-back,
sourceResumeId-gated-on-store-path) with behavioral tests on resolve_resume/
resolve_job/source_resume_id_for_metrics directly — each proves the Store/
Cache miss case errors even when resolve_source/job_source saw text
alongside the id, which the old grep test could not distinguish from a
differently-named alias of the same value. Two thin grep-shaped tests stay,
narrowed to call-site PRESENCE only (execute actually routes through the
pure functions), never branch semantics.

Adds coverage for run_store_job_url/unlinked_run_key: deterministic per
text, distinct per posting, survives normalize_job_url's scheme guard
unchanged, and a store-level retention test (3 unlinked runs of job A + 1
of job B survive prune() intact; a 4th run of A evicts only A's oldest,
never B) pinning the MEDIUM 2 fix directly against PipelineRunStore.

Extends the existing clamp test for the now-clamped resumeId/jobId (LOW 1)
and adds a whitespace-collapse regression for the notification label
(SEC-LOW-2). Every new assertion was mutation-checked (temporarily broken,
confirmed red, reverted) before landing.

* test(pipeline): add strategy_user to the forgery-resistance sweep

tauri-security-reviewer (SEC-LOW-1): strategy_user was the one résumé-
consuming stage prompt missing from every_untrusted_block_is_fenced_and_
forgery_resistant, even though it fences through the same primitive
(prompts.rs::fenced/fenced_artifact) every other stage in the sweep does.
Behavior was already correct; this closes the gap so a future regression
in that stage specifically would be caught.

* test(shared): assert the company-name cap on the résumé-pipeline schema

rust-backend-architect (LOW 2): jobTitle and board both had a dedicated
oversized-value assertion in the text-path cap test; companyName's 512
cap had a Rust-side assertion (clamp_request) but no TS one.

* fix(renderer): stop the tailor-run persist loop and the cross-application run leak

F1 — useTailorPipeline's run-persist effect listed the host-supplied
onRunStarted in its deps with no already-persisted guard. On the real
DocumentsTab/TailorFlow wiring onRunStarted writes a Zustand slice, which
always returns a new object, re-rendering the host, which passes a brand
new arrow back in — an infinite loop that threw "Maximum update depth
exceeded" the instant a run started. Fixed by reading onRunStarted from a
ref (dropped from the deps array entirely) plus a persistedRunRef keyed on
`${runId}|${jobId}` so a re-run of the effect for the same run is a no-op.

F2 — applyRunId/applyRunJobId were reset only inside the
applyForId-mismatch guard, but both apply entry points
(usePostingActions.handleTailor, AutopilotPage.handleApply) set applyForId
to the NEW application's id before navigating, with no compensating clear
of the reconnect target — so the guard was already a no-op by the time the
new application's DocumentsTab (the wizard's default tab) mounted, and its
useResumePipelineSession's lazy useState initializer permanently captured
the stale run id. Fixed by making the reconnect target self-describing:
applyRun: { forId, runId, jobId } | null, read only when
forId === application.id. This is correct on the very first render
(no ordering to get right) instead of only after a reset effect fires.

TailorFlowPersistence.setRunId/setRunJobId collapse into one setRun(ids)
so a reconnect target is always written atomically.

Tests: an unstable-callback (fresh arrow per render) regression at the
hook level plus a DocumentsTab-shaped mount-level test through the real
useTailorPipeline chain for F1; a forId-mismatch + happy-path pair for F2.

* fix(renderer): resume input card's chip label stops misattributing to the default doc

activeDoc fell back to the default saved résumé whenever selectedDocId was
null, so the resting chip showed the default's title even when the
on-screen text (a hand-edit, upload, paste, or profile import) had nothing
to do with it. selectedDocId === null now means "no backing doc, full
stop" for the chip label too, matching the fix already applied to
handleTextChange/handleRemove's doc-id tracking.

Test: a saved doc is selected, then the text is hand-edited — activeDoc
must read undefined, not the (only, default) saved doc.

* fix(renderer): tailor-flow ui polish sweep — indicators, contrast, and the owner's 4-step brief

Frontend/UX review batch against the owner's acceptance bar ("clean ui ux,
not crowded, indicators explaining each section, and when each step is
done it should mark it as done"):

H2 — the 4th step ("remove AI signs") could never actually be SHOWN as
done: the generating panel unmounts the instant the run finishes, before
currentStep could ever reach the step count. The results panel now
renders a compact 4-check "all steps completed" summary on a genuinely
clean finish.

H1/M4 — the thinking bubble now takes defaultExpanded (collapsed by
default in this tight panel, buys back ~200px at the 900x600 floor) and
done={currentStep >= 2} instead of a hardcoded false (it was claiming
"still thinking" forever with a blinking caret on a frozen transcript once
validate/humanize started).

H3 — an mm:ss-since-this-step-started caption on the active row; text
updates survive prefers-reduced-motion since nothing here is a CSS
animation. validate/humanize/repair emit no stream deltas, so without this
the panel read as stalled for its longest phases.

H4 — a run that timed out but still saved a document reports completed
(the backend's timed-out-with-document path); the banner now also shows
when a non-'done' stoppedReason rides along a 'done' runState, instead of
suppressing the caveat entirely. The new "all steps completed" summary
(H2) is gated on the SAME clean-finish check, so a truncated run never
claims all four steps finished.

H5 — needsReview with zero open claims pointed at an empty list ("0
claims need your verdict"). Two independent causes fixed: the frontend
now sums unresolved fabrications across BOTH resume and coverLetter slots
instead of only the active tab's, and a genuinely zero-claim needsReview
now shows honest copy pointing at the quality badge. A cold (no live
session) needsReview also says the run needs reopening instead of
implying in-place interactive controls that aren't wired for it.

H6 — the brand-soft-with-opacity utility never gets the light-scheme class
remap (only the bare class does) — measured 2.38:1 on light, was
invisible-adjacent. Now bare (5.05:1 light) at 10px, doubling as the M5/M2
fix (active step label + its sole sub-line both use the wizard's own
affordance).

H7 — the description/circle-numeral text at low opacity (~4.17:1 light)
and the pending label's opacity (~3.80:1 light) bumped to the repo's own
established floor for sub-14px text, both independently proven to clear
AA by the existing light-scheme-contrast test's math.

H8 — an sr-only state word per row (done/active/pending) plus one live
region announcer for step transitions, mirroring an existing sibling
pattern elsewhere in this tree — an aria-hidden icon was the only state
cue.

H9 — cancelling before any text streamed returned silently to the wizard
(cancelled is terminal, the session cancel sets no error, the banner is
gated on one). A one-line acknowledgement now shows on the configuring
stage while the generation state is cancelled and no error/output exists.

M1 — the run-history strip (~170px, permanently mounted) moved behind a
ghost button + modal, matching the quality badge's own modal pattern
elsewhere in this panel (left as-is).

M3 — a one-line header pins above the streaming pane so a résumé-to-letter
mid-run swap doesn't read as the same document continuing.

M6 — the stage-swap animation wrapper drops focus to the document body on
every stage change; the stage body is now a focus target, focused in an
effect keyed on the stage.

M7/M8/M9 — the failed-run hint, the thinking transcript and its header,
and the cancel button's contrast all bumped to clear AA.

Also (frontend, adjacent finding): a cold entry (no run started or
reconnected this session) derived its status banner from the session
machine's own idle state, always reading as a clean "done" even when the
underlying run was needsReview or failed — it now falls back to this
posting's already-fetched run list for that case.

L-tier: the pipeline-step mapper documents its currently-unreachable
max-depth gap instead of leaving it silent; the stage label's missing-key
fallback now uses the translated coarse state instead of leaking a raw
snake_case stage name; the validate step's description no longer names an
internal stage word; a stray status-tint outlier moved to the repo's
established convention; the generating panel's empty-state test now
asserts the real skeleton marker instead of an incidental layout class.

Contrast numbers (sRGB relative-luminance, alpha-over-background,
matching the repo's own light-scheme contrast test method) were computed
for every change above; every bump was verified to clear 4.5:1 on both
the dark card and the light-remapped surface.

Tests: new/updated coverage across the generating panel, thinking bubble,
results panel, and tailor-flow test suites (elapsed caption, sr-only state
words and announcer, streaming-target header, contrast classes, all-done
summary, the H4 gate, H5's zero-claims and cold-entry branches, the
run-history modal, the H9 hint, M6 focus, and the aggregated open-claims
count). H2's guard was mutation-tested: confirmed red against a reverted
clean-finish check, green against the fix.

* fix(renderer): close the ui-ux-expert re-check on tailor-flow

Small surgical round on the three new HIGHs from the second ui-ux-expert
pass; two were introduced by the prior fix round itself.

N1 — the status Tag's `pipeline.status.${runState}` never had a real key
for 'done'/'error' (the catalog is running/completed/needsReview/failed/
cancelled, TailorRunState is done/needsReview/cancelled/error) — a
timed-out-but-saved run rendered the literal dotted key next to its
"stopped" reason, in both locales. The mock in ResultsPanel.test.tsx could
not have caught this: a key-echoing `t` mock is structurally blind to a
missing key. Fixed with an exhaustive `Record<TailorRunState, …>` map
(PIPELINE_STATUS_KEY, exported) so a future TailorRunState member fails to
type-check until mapped, PLUS a new test file that imports the REAL locale
JSON directly (no i18next, no mock) and asserts every reachable dynamic key
this PR touches resolves to real content in both locales — the swept set:
pipeline.status.*, pipeline.step.state.*, pipeline.step.*.{label,description},
pipeline.step.allDone, autopilot.apply.target.*.

N2 — the M6 stage-body focus effect fired unconditionally, including
against an open ModalShell dialog (useFocusTrap only intercepts Tab, no
focusin re-capture) and on first mount. Two guards added: skip the first
run, and bail when the document's active element is inside
`[aria-modal="true"]`.

N3 — the "all steps completed" row and the streaming-target header were
text-foreground/45 (4.22:1 dark, under the repo's documented <14px floor
of /70). Both bumped to /70 (8.04:1 dark / 6.20:1 light).

Plus the gap both reviewers landed on independently: the live-region
announcer silently no-op'd once currentStep reached the step count
(PIPELINE_STEP_KEYS[currentStep] undefined) — a screen-reader user heard
every step start and never heard the run finish. Now announces
pipeline.step.allDone (already shipped in both locales, previously
unwired), same one-utterance-per-transition guard.

Left alone per the explicit scope note: ThinkingBubble's transcript
contrast, the Cancel button contrast, the elapsed-clock reset on
reconnect, and the cold-entry zero-claims copy — none touched.

Every new guard mutation-tested (revert -> red -> restore -> green):
PIPELINE_STATUS_KEY.done, the mount-skip guard, and the modal-bail guard
all confirmed load-bearing this way.

Gates: pnpm typecheck (whole graph, 13/13), pnpm test (whole graph, 488
files / 7118 tests), pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0, en/de key parity
(0 orphans — no new keys added this round, only existing ones wired).

* fix(renderer): resume input card does not select a doc that never loaded its text

handleSelectSaved called selectDoc(doc.id) unconditionally while onChange
was gated on the doc's text existing — a metadata-only or empty saved
résumé left the editor showing whatever text was already there while
selectedDocId claimed it was backed by the empty doc. An id-first pipeline
request would then resolve server-side to the empty stored text, silently
discarding whatever the user was actually looking at. Same defect class as
the stale-docId bug fixed in f055b899.

Picked "don't select" over CodeRabbit's "fetch the text like
handleFileChange does": the backend's list response already carries the
full text (documents_list serializes the whole DocumentRecord, same source
documents_get_text reads), so a re-fetch would return the identical
(still-empty) string — there is nothing to fetch. onChange and selectDoc
now land together or not at all, matching the auto-fill effect's own
existing pattern. The saved menu is left open on a no-op selection instead
of silently closing, so the user can pick a different entry.

Audited every other selectDoc call site for the same shape (id set without
its matching text): handleTextChange/handleRemove (already fixed for this
exact defect), the auto-fill effect, handleFileChange (fetches text before
calling either), handleSavePaste (saves the ALREADY-displayed value, so
there is no text to load), handleProfileUrlSubmit (always clears to null).
No further instance found.

Test: a metadata-only doc fixture (real id/title, no text) proves
handleSelectSaved is a no-op for it and does not clobber an
already-selected id; mutation-tested (reverted the guard, confirmed both
new tests red, restored, confirmed green).

* fix(renderer): flush a pending inline-edit write on unmount instead of dropping it

editActiveOutput debounces the updateAiGeneration.mutate write by
PERSIST_DEBOUNCE_MS; the unmount cleanup only CLEARED both timers and
returned. Type into the résumé or letter and leave the tab (or let the host
remount DocumentsTab) inside that window and the write never happened — the
local override state dies with the unmount too, so nothing recovers it.
Silent user data loss.

Matches DocumentsTab's own flushJd posture (ApplicationDetailPage/index.tsx)
exactly: the pending payload lives in a ref, captured at schedule time (not
re-read at flush time); one flushPersist function is the sole place a write
fires — the debounce timeout and the unmount cleanup both just call it; a
ref indirection keeps the unmount effect's empty deps honest without a
stale closure over flushPersist/mutate.

Also (CR-8): moved this describe block's vi.useRealTimers() out of each
test body into an afterEach — a failed assertion above the old trailing
call would have skipped it and leaked fake timers into every later test in
the file, an order-dependent green.

Tests: edit -> unmount inside the debounce window -> the write fires with
the pending text; a second test confirms the (now-cleared) timer cannot
double-fire after the unmount flush. Mutation-tested: reverted the flush to
clear-only, confirmed the new test red, restored, confirmed green.

* fix(renderer): widen the i18n sweep to pipeline.stopped.* and assert real (non-empty) copy

Two gaps in the sweep this same file added for N1:

- pipeline.stopped.\${suffix} (ResultsPanel's stopped-reason line) was not
  covered at all — stoppedSuffix() folds any unrecognized backend
  StoppedReason onto STOPPED_SUFFIX's values or UNKNOWN_STOPPED_SUFFIX, so
  the reachable key set is exactly that table, and a missing entry renders
  a dotted key in the banner. This is the same class of bug N1 fixed, in
  the neighbouring key path, that the sweep walked past. Iterated from the
  shared helper's own tables (@/lib/stopped-reason), not a hand-copied
  list, so a variant added there is covered automatically.

- toHaveProperty passes for an empty string, so a key that exists but
  carries no copy (rendering as blank chrome, not a loud failure) slipped
  through silently. Every check now goes through one expectRealCopy
  helper asserting a non-empty string in both locales, not just presence.

Also swept the literal (non-dynamic) keys this PR added to ResultsPanel —
needsReviewTitleEmpty/needsReviewHintEmpty/needsReviewHintCold/
failedTitle/failedHint/cancelledHint/pipeline.runs.title — where the risk
is a typo between the call site and the catalog, the same "renders a
dotted key" failure shape a mocked t() cannot catch. Rewrote the file's
header comment to describe this scope accurately instead of the original
overclaim ("every dynamically-constructed key path").

Mutation-tested both fixes independently against the real locale JSON:
removing pipeline.stopped.runTimeout turns the new sweep case red
(restored); setting it to an empty string turns ONLY the new
non-empty-string check red where the old toHaveProperty would have passed
(restored).

* fix(renderer): repair two test assertions that could not fail for the behavior they claimed

* fix(resume): never delete an unmatched draft project, gate on seed plausibility

Structural rework of the projects-normalization pass per rust-backend-architect
review of caef3d1c (C1 executed reproductions: plain titles + bulleted
achievements; bold titles + bullet achievements; a plain-text draft merging
two projects).

- Rule 1: normalization's write authority now extends only to draft Projects
  entries it can confidently match to a seed. An entry that matches nothing
  is left VERBATIM in its original position, never deleted or invented over
  — the validators still grade whatever it says. A second entry resolving to
  an already-used seed is still an allowed dedup drop.
- Rule 2: seed_projects_for_normalize whole-bails (returns no seeds) when the
  source's Projects section produces ANY seed with no link, no stack and no
  description — the signature of a mis-grouped fragment (a swallowed title,
  an achievement bullet counted as its own entry), which the old
  "any entry-start line" gate could not see (bullets satisfy the entry-start
  rule; the swallowed plain title never becomes a seed).
- Rule 3: build() now also bails the whole pass when a seed the draft never
  matched has its own link present, unattached, somewhere in the draft's
  Projects text — the signature of the DRAFT's own entry grouping merging two
  projects into one (a plain-text draft has no gate at all otherwise).
- Rule 4: seeds_are_plausible now compares only stack entries and links
  against sibling names/links, dropping the description from the haystack —
  a truthful description cross-referencing a sibling project by name no
  longer disables normalization for an honest source.
- Rule 5: every bail records a content-free reason
  (projectsNormalizeSkipped: empty_seed | implausible_seeds |
  draft_parse_disagreement | no_entry_starts | seed_claims_multiple_entries)
  on the draft-stage ledger artifact, so a silent skip is observable.
- Rule 6 (N3): source.rs only strips markdown-link spans it actually captured
  as links before the bare-URL harvest pass; a span the single-URL guard
  skipped keeps its own bare URL(s) reachable instead of deleting them.
- Additional guard beyond the seven rules: while testing the primary
  "N projects collapse into one seed" shape from a fully plain-text source,
  neither the empty-seed nor the plausibility gate catches it when the
  resulting single seed's merged links/description both happen to be
  non-empty (no sibling to compare against). build() now also bails
  (seed_claims_multiple_entries) when a seed the link-fallback matches to a
  SECOND, differently-named draft entry — the direct signature of one seed
  having swallowed multiple projects' links, distinct from an ordinary
  same-name dedup. Flagged here since it goes past the literal seven rules.
- max: output-preserving; the dropped-metric now also counts a dedup
  collision it silently missed before (from the previous review round).

* fix(ai): distinguish a rejected health probe from "still checking"

PR #989 CodeRabbit round 1, two MAJOR findings.

1. useCanUseAI read only `useSystemHealth().data`, never `isError`. A
   REJECTED health query (network blip, backend hiccup) leaves `data`
   undefined forever (retry: false) — indistinguishable from "still
   pending" in the local-server branch (permanent, silent "checking"
   that never resolves) and silently misreported as `installCli` ("go
   install the CLI") in the cli-agent branch, since `?? false` treated
   undefined-from-error the same as undefined-from-loading. A consumer
   rendering AiSetupHint with no reason then fell back to its own
   default (`aiSetup.addApiKey`) — wrong for every affected provider
   kind. Now three-way: pending (no reason, "checking") → error (new
   `healthUnavailable` reason) → settled (the real gate). New
   aiSetup.healthUnavailable en+de keys ("Couldn't check AI status. Try
   again in a moment." / "KI-Status konnte nicht geprüft werden.
   Versuche es in Kürze erneut."), wired into both AiSetupHint's
   MESSAGE_KEY and AISystemStatus's own copy.

2. AISystemStatus.test.tsx's reason→key table (added when `startOllama`
   shipped) never grew a row for it — a silent AI_REASON_KEY drift back
   to the addApiKey fallback would have stayed green. Adds both the
   startOllama and the new healthUnavailable rows.

Coverage: useCanUseAI.test.tsx gains a rejected-health-query case for
both consuming branches (local-server, cli-agent).

Mutation-tested per the coordinator's exact asks: dropping startOllama
from AI_REASON_KEY turns its table row red (falls back to addApiKey);

body around or move a page break.

Monogram sets a pale accent square carrying up to two initials beside a

whichever resume template is active and a light accent would put white on
near-white -- and the 85% lightening is the same `band_tint_hex` the DOCX side
already uses, which is what lets the two formats show one tint.

The brief said to mirror how Banded gates its band under ats_mode. It does not:
`ats_mode` never reached the letter path at all. `render_letter_pdf` had no
`ats` parameter, `LetterOpts` had no `ats` field, and `pdf/mod.rs` read

`data.opts.ats`, and Banded's band is gated on it too: the discipline has to be
uniform or the toggle is a lie. Under ATS mode Sidebar drops the rail and stacks
the letterhead in one plain column, Monogram drops the device entirely (its
initials are real text -- extraction read "JS Jane Smith", two characters of
noise ahead of the candidate's own name), and Banded drops the band. No layout

`ats` is a required parameter on `parse_cover_letter` rather than a defaulted
field: an ATS toggle that silently fails to reach the renderer looks exactly
like one that works, which is how this gap survived four letter layouts.

Structural elements gate on `data.opts`, never on the layout id -- the DE DIN
Betreff renders and the US subject does not, from the identical layout.

DOCX: `LetterDocxStyle` gains rows for both, read off each `.typ` feature by
feature. Sidebar's rail has no DOCX equivalent at all (a text box or a
two-column table would be exactly the multi-column trap the export avoids), so
it becomes the same shaded name paragraph Banded uses, with the contact LEFT at
the margin. That alignment is why `contact_align` is now a stored field instead
of a function of "centred or right": Sidebar and Monogram left-align the contact
while leaving the name left too, which the derived version could not express --
and inherit-by-omission is the defect that took four review rounds on Navy.

Review round 1 on the sidebar/monogram layouts. Five findings, all in the two
files this PR added.

Hyphenation (ruling 1, scoped): both new layouts now set `hyphenate: false`.
Typst turns hyphenation on with `justify`, and a hyphenated break puts a real
break in the PDF text layer -- "microservices architecture" extracts as
"architec-ture" and an ATS tokenising on whitespace loses the keyword. Justify
stays. The guard lives in `letter_lower`, the choke point every extraction in
this file already flows through, so no test can regress it -- but gated on a
`NO_SOFT_HYPHEN_LAYOUTS` roster of the two new layouts, because the four SHIPPED
ones still hyphenate and a family-wide assert would go red on them today. The
roster grows when the sweep lands.

Correcting my own measurement, per the critic: of the three U+00AD-adjacent
breaks I reported, only ONE is a genuine soft-hyphen break. The others are hard
hyphens ("end-to-end"), which Typst tags with /ActualText and a conforming
extractor recovers -- asserting on those would be asserting on a non-defect, so
the guard checks U+00AD only. And the shipped family is SIX .typ files, not the
five I wrote: letter_navy.typ was already there.

Initials, two defects in one function. It searched each token for its first
alphanumeric ANYWHERE, so a token that merely contained a letter contributed
one: "Jane Smith (they/them)" was JT. And it had no notion of a title, so
"Dr. Jane Smith" was DS and the German "Dipl.-Ing. Max Müller" was DM. A token
now has to START with an alphanumeric, and a token that abbreviates a WORD (two
or more letters before its period) is a title or qualification and is dropped --
while a single-letter initial keeps counting, so "J. Smith" stays JS instead of
degrading to S.

My test for the first of those was a false positive and the critic was right
about why: the fixture was "(she/her)" and the expected "JS" is ALSO what the
broken code produced, because its S came from "she". Refixtured to
"(they/them)", where correct and broken are distinguishable (JS vs JT), which is
what made the mutation run meaningful.

Device on a letterhead-less letter: the PDF-side name falls back to the first
LINE when no candidate name is supplied, and three renderer call sites pass an
empty one -- so on a letter that opens at the salutation the device rendered
"DM", from "Dear Hiring Manager,". Reproduced exactly. The DOCX renderer already
refused to treat an opening line as a name; `letterhead_initials` is the PDF
side of the same guard, scoped to the DEVICE because what `letterhead.name`
should show there is a separate pre-existing question across all six layouts.

Sidebar's contact links go through `place()` with a negative dx into the margin,
which is the documented annotation-loss shape. They survive -- but nothing said
so, and a dropped /Annots entry is invisible to every text assertion, so it is
pinned now in both modes.

DIN 5008: the header claimed market conventions were honoured while the
recipient block sits at 62mm, so a DE letter cannot show its address through a
window envelope. Chose the honest comment over a locale-conditional rail, and
not only because that is heavy -- it is unachievable. Form B needs the
Anschriftenfeld clear from 20mm, and a rail narrower than that cannot hold a
contact line at 9.5pt. DIN compliance and a contact rail want the same strip of
paper, so Sidebar is a screen/attachment layout and the comment now says to pick
Classic or Navy for the envelope.

Also: the monogram device was a bound `#let`, so it read
`data.letterhead.initials` when the binding evaluated -- before the
`"initials" in data.letterhead` check below it. The guard was dead. It takes the
initials as a parameter now, so the read happens only on the checked branch.

Every new guard was mutation-tested: removing `hyphenate: false` fails four
tests, the old token rule fails the pronoun and title tests (DS vs JS), removing
the salutation guard yields DM and MG, and dropping the `link()` wrapper fails
with `found []`.

* chore(deps): drop the no-op reqwest rustls-native-certs feature

reqwest 0.13.1 exposed `rustls-native-certs` only as the implicit feature
of an optional dependency it never references in its own source, so
enabling it changed nothing: OS trust roots already arrive through
`rustls-platform-verifier` (pulled by reqwest's `rustls` feature) and
through the system stack behind `native-tls`.

reqwest 0.13.2 removed the optional dependency, which turns the stale
entry into a hard resolve error. Unblocks any bump that floats reqwest
past 0.13.1.

* chore(deps): bump sentry 0.42 -> 0.49 with tauri-plugin-sentry 0.6

The coordinated bump dependabot could not do. tauri-plugin-sentry 0.6
builds against sentry 0.49, so the plugin-only PR (#972) duplicated
sentry/sentry-core/sentry-types in the lock; both sides move together
here. sentry-rust-minidump follows transitively, 0.13 -> 0.17 (its
lib.rs is byte-identical between the two, so no supervisor API change).

Re-verified the four traps the Cargo.toml comment block records:

* Single copy — sentry, sentry-core, sentry-types all resolve to exactly
  one 0.49.1, shared by the app, the plugin, and the minidump crate. The
  stale reqwest 0.12 lock entry sentry 0.42 dragged along is gone, so
  reqwest is now single-version too (0.13.4).
* Transport — `ureq` and `native-tls` still exist as features in 0.49
  and still select `UreqHttpTransport`; sentry's resolved deps are
  httpdate, native-tls, sentry-*, ureq, with no reqwest and no tokio.

* Capability — `sentry:default` still expands to allow-envelope +

* Init + consent — init still runs before tauri::Builder and still forks
  the supervisor from the same call. `ClientOptions` became
  #[non_exhaustive] in 0.49, so the struct literal moves to the builder;
  every field keeps its previous value.

No paired npm package exists: the browser SDK is a js_init_script inside
the crate, so there is nothing on the JS side to bump.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(deps): reconcile the lock after rebasing over the dependabot bumps

* fix(crash-reporting): enforce consent and drop opaque envelopes at the wire

Security review found real, new egress in tauri-plugin-sentry 0.6, and a
claim of mine that was simply false. `before_send` is not the last hop:
it has exactly one call site in sentry-core 0.49.1 (client/mod.rs:383,
inside the capture_event preparation). Anything handed to
`Client::send_envelope` reaches the transport with no callback between.

The plugin uses that door. When a renderer envelope fails to parse — it
routinely does, because @sentry/vite-plugin's debug-ID injection writes
a `debug_meta` sourcemap image sentry-rust cannot deserialize — 0.6
rebuilds it via `Envelope::from_bytes_raw` and calls `send_envelope`
(commands.rs:30-35). Those bytes live in a private `Items::Raw` that
`to_writer` copies to the socket verbatim, so no redaction of ours can
reach inside. Plugin 0.5 dropped them; 0.6 ships them.

So the guarantee moves to the only place that sees every byte. A
`GuardedTransportFactory` wraps the SDK's own DefaultTransportFactory
(ureq under our features) and enforces, per envelope:

  * consent, re-read from an atomic mirror of the consent file. This
    also closes the mid-session opt-out hole: `Hub::current()` is
    thread-local, so `disable_current` only unbound the calling thread,
    and the plugin's own Client clone in Tauri state never consults a
    hub at all.
  * opaque envelopes dropped, restoring 0.5's semantics. A payload we
    cannot inspect is one we cannot redact; the privacy guarantee
    outranks the sourcemap edge case. Counted and logged content-free.

flush/shutdown delegate, so the supervisor's pre-exit flush still works.

Also here:
  * `.enable_logs(false)` / `.enable_metrics(false)`. Both default to
    TRUE in 0.49 (0.42 had them off) and the field is not cfg-gated, so
    any future crate enabling `sentry/logs` would unify the feature in
    and open the pipe silently.
  * deny.toml bans `failspot/enabled` — a fault-injection crate riding
    in under the crash reporter, inert as locked (its lock entry has no
    dependencies, so `dep:flagset` is off) and it must stay that way.
  * Corrected three comments this falsified: lib.rs on renderer events
    inheriting before_send, the module docs on where redaction is
    enforced, and `disable_current`'s claim to drop "every subsequent
    event".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(crash-reporting): stop overclaiming what the options test guards

Mutation-checking my own test found one assertion that does not guard
what its doc said it did. Deleting `.send_default_pii(false)` leaves the
test green, because `false` is also `ClientOptions::default()` — so that
line catches a wrong value but not a deleted call, and no test could
distinguish the two.

The other six were each verified by deletion: transport, before_send,
before_breadcrumb, enable_logs, enable_metrics, server_name all turn the
test red when their builder call is removed.

feat(pipeline): phase 4 — the max generation depth (#970)

* feat(pipeline): max-depth section artifact types

The typed answers one max-depth section call may return, plus the seeds a
section is generated FROM. The split between SectionSeed and the *Out
types is the core rule expressed as types: identity, project links and
education lines are seeded from the source and the model authors only the
presentation. JudgeItem deliberately has no severity field, so the
Warning-only cap is structural rather than a filter.

* feat(pipeline): per-section generation for max depth

One structured call per resume section, in a fixed source-gated order, with
every answer filtered before it is kept: unbacked citations dropped, a
skill the source never states removed, an education entry that is not a
verbatim copy discarded, and a project's name/links/stack re-seeded from
the source whatever the model returned. The fan-out checks the run
deadline between calls and treats one section's failure as one section,
never as the run's.

The projects-format primitives (entry boundaries, link detection, the
description-line cap) are re-exported from validate::content rather than
re-implemented, so the generator and the checks that grade its output
cannot disagree about a truthful document.

* feat(pipeline): assemble the max-depth sections into a resume body

The finished sections become the SAME plain-text body the quality draft
produces, so validate, repair, the report, the editor and the exporters
see one shape at both depths. The layout is code-owned: the identity line
is rendered in the form split_entry reads back, consecutive employment
entries share one heading, and the projects ladder renders exactly the
three shapes consistency.project_structure accepts — a project the source
never described gets the compact link line, never a filler blurb.

The progressive stream appends the same bytes the document will carry, so
what the user watches build is what the run assembles.

* feat(pipeline): run the staged pipeline at max depth

max_pipeline() + MAX_STAGES, Budget::RESUME_MAX and its own run deadline,
and the L3 wiring that lets one execute() serve both depths through three
lookups instead of two copies of the shell. RunHooks gains the
section-wise half: per-section pipeline:stage events with sectionKey
filled (validated by the generated grammar) and the progressive document
stream on the existing ai:stream channel, display-only at both depths.

The max deadline deliberately does NOT buy the re-ask worst case the
quality one does: 3h20m is a backstop no user sits through, and a max run
stopped mid-fan-out keeps the sections it already assembled.

* feat(pipeline): the max-depth llm judge, warning-only and skippable

One structured call reviewing the finished document, contributing advisory
judge.* Warnings to the report. Three structural caps: JudgeItem has no
severity field, every issue is built with Severity::Warning written at the
construction site, and every failure mode (provider error, expired
deadline, refused daily cap, unparseable answer) records a reason code and
returns Ok — the judge can never fail a run.

Deviation from the settled stage order, with the reason: the judge runs
AFTER repair, not between validate and repair. repair replaces ctx.report
with the one it re-validated, so notes merged in earlier are dropped on
exactly the documents that were repaired, and a quote taken before a
repair names text the finished document no longer contains.

* feat(pipeline): regenerate one max-depth entry from its persisted artifacts

At max depth the strategy and evidence artifacts are persisted in FULL
alongside their counts, in the DB event row only — ADR-027 is the LOG
boundary and the log lines stay counts-only. A later 'regenerate this
role' click reads them back and rebuilds exactly that entry through the
same generate_one and the same assemble the run used, splicing only its
line range so the other roles cannot change.

Every miss is soft: a quality run, a non-experience key, a run older than
the detail, an artifact the store's clamp truncated, or an entry the
document no longer has all fall back to the whole-section rewrite. A click
must not fail because an optimization was unavailable.

* style(pipeline): satisfy clippy on the max-depth tests

assertions_on_constants: two shipped budgets compared at runtime prove
nothing a const block does not prove at build time. filter_next: rfind.

* feat(renderer): enable max generation depth

The staged pipeline runs max now, so the depth flag flips and the panel
sends the depth the user picked instead of the quality literal. The
unavailable note follows the same rule as the run: both staged depths
need the same server-resolved inputs, so it shows for either.

* feat(renderer): map the max-depth stages onto the run machine

`sections` and `assemble` are max depth's split of `draft`; `llm_judge`
runs last, after repair, and reads the finished document, so it maps to
the checking state rather than the repairing one. A max run therefore
ends its stage trail in `validating` — still busy, because no stage
event may ever end a run.

* feat(renderer): fold per-section progress off the stage stream

Max depth reports each section through the same `pipeline:stage`
channel, so the session hook folds `sectionKey` + phase into a
per-section map. Only states an event proves are written: `queued` is
not observable (the wire carries the STAGE's index/total and the section
counts ride in the persisted artifact), and neither validate nor repair
attributes its counts to a section, so verdicts stay with the report.

* feat(renderer): live section timeline for a max-depth run

A checklist of the sections the run has actually reported, in generation
order, hosted next to the stage dots. No placeholder rows: the roster
depends on the strategy's company plan and never reaches the renderer,
so a pre-drawn list would name sections that may never be generated. An
experience entry is numbered rather than given a company name the
content-free wire never carried.

* docs(renderer): the display-only stream carries max depth's assembly too

Nothing was gating the stream on depth, so nothing needed ungating: both
depths ride one `ai:stream` under the run's umbrella job. The doc said
"the draft stage's deltas", which is only half of what arrives now, and
a test pins that the pane renders the progressively assembled text
without a branch — still display-only.

* feat(renderer): label the max-depth judge's remarks as model-written

A `judge.*` message is the model's own prose about this document, not a
label for a fixed check, so the panel renders it verbatim: the namespace
short-circuits the catalog lookup structurally, before `i18n.exists`,
rather than relying on nobody adding the key. It carries a provenance
badge — the note is free text derived from an untrusted posting, and it
stays an inert text node. Per-section repair attribution still does not
exist at either depth; the note in SectionVerdicts now says so.

* feat(shared): a max-depth run deadline the client can be held above

Mirrors `timeouts::max_run_deadline` (6900 s fixed + one effort-scaled
pass, 7200–7800 s) so the renderer has a bound that stays ABOVE the
backend's at every tier — the side that knows why a run stopped has to
give up first. Hand-mirrored rather than generated, because gen:ipc does
not emit the Rust constant; the per-tier table is pinned as literals on
both sides so the pair cannot drift silently.

* fix(pipeline): f2 — join a per-entry regenerate on identity, never on position

* fix(renderer): give the section ladder the `done` rung it needs

`PipelineSectionState` never had `done`, so the fold that writes it on a
`sections` finish did not type-check — vitest runs esbuild and said
nothing; `tsc` caught it. Folding onto `checking` instead would claim a
check that has not started, so the type gains the rung the plan's ladder
always described. `max` is also a runnable stored depth now, so the
preference coercion needs a value from outside the vocabulary to stay

* fix(pipeline): a run whose posting was deleted mid-flight abandons its own output

trail because the pre-purge events were already gone. Confirmed by running
it: purge, one event appended into the gap, terminal upsert, row back with 1

* fix: harden json extraction and structured-prompt assembly against hostile model output

Security review found the latent complete_structured surface exploitable
before its first caller lands. extract_json committed to the first fenced
block before any deserialization attempt, so a triple-backtick inside a JSON
string value (a job posting with a code fence echoed into a field) hijacked
a fully valid response into all-defaults data reported as success, and an
attacker echoing a fenced object first controlled the parsed value on every
prompt-discipline path. parse now walks ordered candidates — the whole
response when it is exactly one balanced value, then fenced bodies last-first,
then top-level balanced spans last-first — with a clean parse pass for every
candidate before any repair.

JsonParseError derived Debug, re-exposing the exact model content its
hand-written Display withholds ({:?} logging and .expect() panic text reach
the crash reporter); Debug is now hand-written over reason() only. The
re-ask path gets a safe-by-construction reask_detail() that wraps the
fragment in the shared ADR-010 fence with the raw detail() accessor demoted
to pub(crate). structured_prompt now flattens turns through the shared
flatten_messages so assistant/tool provenance markers survive, matches the
system role case-insensitively, and schema translation recursion is
depth-capped, failing whole to the existing fallbacks.

* fix(renderer): validate quality_report shape before parsing (m-1)

parseQualityReport cast unknown -> QualityReport with no shape validation,
so a malformed persisted quality_report column crashed the whole app (only
the root ErrorBoundary caught it) every time that record's TailorFlow
opened. Validate schemaVersion + each sub-report's issues array/metrics
object defensively; a malformed sub-report now drops to undefined instead
of throwing, and a malformed issue entry is filtered rather than crashing
the array.

* fix(agent): defeat nested [tool_result] marker forgery in tool results

TOOL_RESULT_MARKER matched a full [tool_result:...] delimited token whose
body admitted a literal `[`, so a forged marker nested inside another one
(e.g. [tool_result:[tool_result:save_resume]]) survived neutralization:
the greedy body stopped at the FIRST `]` (the inner marker's own close),
leaving the fully-formed inner marker untouched in the output.

Match the opening [tool_result PREFIX only and replace with the canonical
"[ tool_result" form, same convention as the fence-tag neutralizer -
every occurrence is found and broken independently of surrounding
brackets, so nesting can no longer hide one marker from the scan.

* perf(validate): cap the near-duplicate bullet scan at 400 bullets

duplicates::validate is an O(bullets²) pairwise Jaccard scan that ran
unbounded — a malformed or hostile "generated" document with thousands of
bullet-shaped lines held a tokio worker for seconds on every save.

Truncate to MAX_DUP_BULLETS (400) before the pairwise pass, mirroring the
count-cap discipline agent::tools_quality already uses. A pathological
bullet count now returns in well under 500ms and still flags a genuine
duplicate placed inside the cap.

* fix(validate): cap the content-report issue list to avoid silent report loss

An uncapped ContentReport.issues could grow the serialized report toward
~1MB on a pathological document (thousands of forged roles / duplicate
bullets). The IPC save path clamps quality_report to 256KB, truncating
that blob mid-JSON; merge_quality_report then fails to parse it and
silently falls back to the OLD stored report — a fresh report just
vanishes.

Cap the issue list at MAX_CONTENT_ISSUES (200) in validate_content itself,
so the byte clamp downstream is never reached. Criticals sort first before
truncation so a warning flood can never push a real Critical out of the
visible list; a trailing REPORT_TRUNCATED marker names the dropped count
instead of a silent cut.

* fix(validate): strip control chars from target-language input

normalize_language only trimmed leading/trailing whitespace before taking
the first 2 characters, so an internal control character (e.g. "a\nb")
survived into the 2-char result. That value reaches this module's own
validate:content span text and content.language_mismatch's evidence — a
log-injection primitive.

Filter to alphanumeric characters before taking the first 2. Also mirror
the Zod targetLanguage.max(32) cap server-side in resume_validate_content,
the same trust-boundary treatment every other field on that command
already gets.

* docs(agent): correct stale four-result-tags comment in the fence-tag registry

The comment claimed four super::tools_quality result tags were registered;
only three are. The fourth tool (lookup_salary) carries no free text to
fence and returns via envelope_result instead. Fix the comment so a future
fenced salary result isn't wrongly assumed already covered.

* fix(ai-generations): clamp quality_report on the bundle import path

The IPC save path already clamps quality_report to QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES
before persisting, but AiGenerationStore::import (a restored backup bundle
- an equally untrusted, user-supplied file) wrote the bundle's quality_report
straight to the column with no cap at all.

Move QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES into the data layer as the single source of
truth for both write paths, and clamp it in import too.

* docs: point at the content-issue code roster instead of copying its count

* fix(ai-generate): clear stale report before regenerating

handleGenerate cleared resumeOut/coverOut/buffers but never the quality
report, so the 'both'-mode progressive-reveal window (stage done while
the cover still streams) rendered the previous generation's report
against the new resume until persist recomputed one.

* fix(ai-generate): guard recheck against a mid-flight session reset

handleRecheck awaited validateContent.mutateAsync then unconditionally
called onReportChange with a stale closure's report/currentOutput — a
Reset during the in-flight call could re-inject a report into an
already-cleared session. Add an epoch ref bumped whenever meta/
sourceResume/jobAd change, checked before onReportChange fires.

* fix(quality-report): map the truncated-report code and add a message fallback

The synthetic report.truncated code had no i18n key, so it rendered the
generic quality.fallback sentence plus a bare count as evidence. Add
quality.issue.report.truncated (en + de) and make messageFor() fall
back to the Rust-authored issue.message before quality.fallback, so
any future unmapped code degrades to something meaningful.

* fix(validate): key accented project links without a utf-8 boundary panic

canonical_link stripped the scheme with `&s[..8]`, a fixed BYTE offset, so
any project URL whose 7th/8th byte fell inside a multibyte char aborted the
process: `www.café-berlin.de`, `http://éxample.com` and `ab.com/éx` all
panicked with "byte index 8 is not a char boundary". The release profile is
panic = "abort", so the app died mid-generation, before the document was
saved — a German or French project domain was enough to trigger it.

Byte-compare the scheme prefix on `as_bytes()` and only slice once the
prefix is known to be that (pure-ASCII) scheme. Audited the rest of
canonical_link and urls_in: every other boundary already comes from a
char-aware API (`trim`, `trim_end_matches`, `split_once`, regex match
spans), so this was the only fixed-offset cut.

Covered by a canonical_link unit test with a straddling char at each
boundary the function cuts at (2-, 3- and 4-byte widths), the three
reproducer URLs run through the full validate_content path, and an accented
link in the en source/paraphrase fixture pair so the fixture suite carries
it permanently.

* fix(agent): order criticals first before compacting the issue list

compact_content_report took the first MAX_ISSUES issues in EMISSION order,
but validate_content emits in check order, not severity order. A draft that
tripped 20+ Warnings before a late check therefore dropped the Critical
itself — ats.header_in_body is emitted near the end — while the summary
still reported `criticals: 1`. The model saw a count it had no issue to act
on.

Stable-sort Criticals ahead of everything else before the cap; within each
severity the emission order is preserved, and the counts still reflect the
full report rather than the surfaced slice.

feat: add exa as a fallback web-search backend for company research (#961)

* feat: add a pluggable web-search backend with exa as the fallback

Company research runs on the active AI provider's own web search, which leaves a
whole population with nothing: local Ollama without an ollama.com account key,
every `openai-compatible` gateway, and any provider whose search isn't wired up.
They get a silently empty brief, and the cover letter is written with no company
knowledge - indistinguishable from one written with a full brief.

The seam was already there. `research.rs` is provider-agnostic (SearchResult,
the query builders, the synth prompts, the injection guard), and the three
`ollama_research*` functions were each "search -> if empty return '' ->
synthesize with the provider's own model". Only the search step was ever
Ollama-specific.

So this extracts that step behind a `WebSearcher` trait, moves the three
pipelines to `search/` as `searched_research*`, and adds `ExaSearcher`
(api.exa.ai/search, `ai:exa` key). All three research facets - company, salary,
per-question answers - gain the fallback at once.

Selection is FALLBACK-ONLY and decided from configuration before any call: a
provider that can already search keeps using its own, even with an Exa key
stored, so nobody silently starts paying a second vendor. A native search that
runs and returns empty is NOT retried against Exa - one pass, one search, one
vendor sees the query. `resolve_search_backend` is a pure predicate so that
policy is testable, and inverting it fails a test.

Synthesis deliberately stays on the user's own model. Exa's own answer endpoint
would be fewer calls but would bypass both `SYNTH_SYSTEM`'s prompt-injection
guard (search results are attacker-reachable text) and the `is_no_info` filter.

The fallback lands on the trait's DEFAULT `research()`, so providers with native
search override it and are untouched, and a new provider with no search inherits
it for free - no per-provider change either way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: enforce the generation concurrency cap on the path the app uses

`AI_GENERATE_CONCURRENCY_MAX = 3` was enforced on `ai_generate`, but the
tailoring flow calls `generate_pipeline`, which acquired nothing: no rate
window, no concurrency slot, and no per-provider daily charge. A support bundle
shows the result - six user-initiated runs producing SEVEN concurrent streams,
ending in a provider 429 that discarded nine minutes of already-generated work.

`generate_pipeline` now charges the daily ceiling at admission and takes a
concurrency slot inside its spawned task, so the slot is held for the whole
stream and released on drop.

It uses the new `Limiter::acquire_queued` rather than `acquire`: every call is a
deliberate click on Generate, so the 4th waits its turn instead of being thrown
away. Both admission styles draw on ONE per-command semaphore - two independent
mechanisms would have reproduced the same "cap enforced somewhere else" bug.
The queue is depth-bounded, so it cannot itself become the unbounded resource.

Renderer: `awaitAiStream` re-arms its deadline while `jobs.get` reports
`queued`. That deadline bounds the stream, not the wait for a slot; without
this a queued generation fails on a timeout it never had a chance to beat,
having never sent a request. It still fires normally once the job is running,
so a genuinely stuck job is still caught.

Both release paths are mutation-tested: neutering `QueueSlot::drop` fails the
cancel-safety test, leaking a permit fails four, and dropping the re-arm fails
the queued-deadline test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop sending an embedding model to ollama's chat endpoint

Every HTTP 400 in a reported support bundle - eight of them - was
`provider=ollama model=qwen3-embedding:8b endpoint=/api/chat`, one per scraped
job ad. An embedding model on the chat endpoint is unconditionally rejected.

The chain: `translate_text` (job-ad translation, which runs on every scrape)
reads the EMBEDDING config to find a local provider, then asks
`reachable_chat_model` for a model. That forwarded `ollama::reachable_model`,
which returned `/api/tags`'s first entry unconditionally - it was written as a
health probe ("is Ollama up, and does it have anything") and reused as if it
answered "give me a model that can chat". A user whose first entry is an
embedding model gets a guaranteed 400 on every ad.

`first_chat_model` now skips embedding-only models and returns None when the
user has nothing else installed, so the caller skips translation instead of
issuing a request the daemon will always reject. The filter is a name heuristic
because `/api/tags` carries no capability field - `details.family` is `bert` for
nomic/mxbai but the base family for qwen3-embedding - and the ceiling plus its
upgrade path (`/api/show` capabilities) is written at the function.

It was also invisible: `translate_text` returns the untranslated original on any
error, so the only trace was an `ok=false` span at INFO. Both fallback paths now
warn, which is how this would have been found from the bundle alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: retry a stream's handshake on a transient 429 instead of losing the run

The 429 that killed a generation in a reported session was never retried. The
retry module was wired only into the one-shot complete/embed calls, on the
reasoning that "a mid-stream restart would duplicate already-emitted deltas".

That reasoning does not cover the case it excluded. A non-2xx STATUS arrives
from the request/response handshake, before a single delta has been read, so a
retry there re-sends a request that emitted nothing. There is no output to
duplicate. Treating it as terminal is what turned one provider rate-limit into a
discarded nine-minute generation.

All four streaming adapters now send through `send_stream_with_retry`: the same
bounded loop, with a higher backoff ceiling (30s vs 8s) because the alternative
to waiting is throwing away work the user has already waited minutes for. A
genuinely terminal 4xx is still not retried, the attempt budget is unchanged,
and nothing restarts a stream that has already produced output.

Retries also log at WARN now - a provider pushing back is exactly the context
you want when a generation later fails outright, and at DEBUG it never reached
the log file.

* fix: let each provider own its sampling values instead of the renderer

The renderer picked a temperature per task step and sent it to whatever model
happened to be configured. That is wrong on most of them now. Non-default
temperature, top_p or top_k returns 400 on every request to Claude 4.7 and
later, thinking or not. OpenAI reasoning models reject temperature. Google says
to remove the parameters from Gemini 3 requests entirely and documents that a
temperature below 1.0 causes looping. Six of eight families publish one number
per model with no task dimension at all, so the per-step table was tuning an
axis no vendor supports.

Gemini already had a guard for this and it was dead code. It withheld the
adapter's own fallback only when the caller supplied nothing, but the renderer
always supplied something, so every request looked like a deliberate user
choice. The onboarding default is a Gemini 3 model, so new users hit the
documented degradation case on their first generation.

The renderer now sends an intent and each adapter owns the numbers, behind a
trait method whose default sends nothing at all. Omitting is correct or better
on Claude, OpenAI reasoning models, Gemini 3, native Ollama, which inherits the
modelfile, and vLLM gateways, which inherit generation_config. An unknown model
on an unknown provider therefore falls through to that provider's own defaults,
so a new model still needs no code. Anthropic needed no change: its fail-safe
was already right, and the work was generalising it to the other four adapters.

Explicit values still win, so the per-model temperature sliders keep working.
prose_grounded keeps presence_penalty off the surfaces that write factual
claims about the candidate to a third party, since that penalty pushes toward
new topics. Ollama Cloud is special-cased because its openai-compatible layer
hardcodes 1.0 when a value is omitted, overriding the modelfile.

Also routes the job analysis and the inline rewrite through the resolver. Both
used bare literals, so the analysis slider changed metadata extraction and not
the analysis it is named for.

* fix: key the resume name rule on the first line with content, not raw line 0

index. PDF extraction routinely emits a leading blank line before the header
text, so the real name landed at index 1, missed the rule, matched

into a section named after the candidate while header.name and header.contact
stayed empty and apply_to_header refilled them from the contact profile — the

be a real index into all_lines, since an out-of-bounds range must not read as
a vacuously-true empty slice.

* fix: repair pdf link anchors corrupted before the utf-16 decoder landed

pdf_text_string in #955 stopped new corruption but could not touch text
already written. A PDF text string is UTF-16BE behind a FE FF BOM, and reading
it with from_utf8_lossy rendered the BOM as two U+FFFD followed by every
character interleaved with its NUL high byte, so stored link anchors read as
mojibake and matched no project title, leaving every link heaped at the end of
the section instead of on its own entry.

The shape is losslessly reversible, so repair_utf16_mojibake drops the doubled
replacement chars and the NULs, gated on the string containing a NUL at all,
which is never legitimate in stored document text. Two appended migrations
rewrite only NUL-bearing rows in documents.text and in ai_generations'
resume_text and cover_letter_text. A per-row failure warns rather than
propagating: rolling back would undo every other row's repair and leave
user_version wedged, retrying the same failure on every future startup.

Also fixes two pre-existing tests that identified their target as
MIGRATIONS.len() - 1. Appending anything silently pointed them at the wrong
migration, which is the trap a position-indexed list sets for every future
append.

* fix: scope the mojibake repair to the shape it can actually reconstruct

Review round on the repair migrations.

The per-row UPDATE error is propagated instead of swallowed. Swallowing did
not do what its comment claimed: on a disk-full or IO error SQLite auto-rolls
back the enclosing transaction, so the loop continued in autocommit and the
following PRAGMA user_version committed on its own, durably marking the
migration applied while the row stayed corrupt and was never retried. Store
opens are already non-fatal in lib.rs, so propagating costs a session, not the
app.

The repair is now anchored on the corruption's own shape rather than stripping
every doubled replacement char and every NUL in the row. It requires the BOM
marker followed by a NUL, then consumes only (NUL, ASCII) pairs it can
reconstruct. A resume body carrying two adjacent unmapped-glyph markers no
longer has them silently deleted, which fused words on the html and rtf import
paths, and a UTF-16 anchor with non-ASCII code units is left alone rather than
turned into plausible garbage with its markers erased, since those bytes are
still a faithful image of the payload and remain recoverable.

Repaired documents also clear keywords_json and indexed. Rewriting the text
while leaving the cached keywords and the embedding pinned to the corrupt
version would have scored the resume forever against text it no longer
contains. Both migrations snapshot the affected rows first, and the insert,
update and import paths repair on write, so restoring a bundle exported before
this fix cannot re-inject the corruption.

feat: résumé trim panel, pdf link-anchor decode fix, and effort picker on every model surface (#955)

* fix: decode pdf text strings as utf-16 so link anchors stop arriving as mojibake

A PDF text string (PDF 32000-1 §7.9.2.2) is not UTF-8 — it is either
PDFDocEncoded or UTF-16BE behind a FE FF byte-order mark, and Typst, LaTeX and
Word all emit the UTF-16BE form for annotation /Contents. Reading those bytes
with from_utf8_lossy turned every link anchor into the BOM rendered as two
replacement chars followed by each ASCII character interleaved with its NUL
high byte.

That mojibake travelled: the extractor wrote it into the \n---\n reference
block, and packages/prompts/src/generate/links could no longer match an anchor
to its project title, so every link fell through to the unmatched-links append
path and landed in a block of its own instead of on its project.

Adds pdf_text_string() — UTF-16BE, UTF-16LE (not spec-legal but real producers
emit it), UTF-8-with-BOM, and BOM-less bytes passed through unchanged. Applied
at all three sites that shared the shape: the /Contents anchor, the /URI, and
validate/mod.rs's round-trip URL check.

* feat: index documents automatically, and stop the index strip reading as a chore

Reported as "I have to go to AI settings and press the indexing button after
uploading a résumé". Tracing it first: that was never true. `match_resume`
already embeds lazily when it finds no usable vector and caches the result, so
the Settings button is a pre-warm, not a prerequisite. What it actually cost was
a slow first match and a status strip that looked like a task list.

Three parts.

**Say what is true.** The strip said "N documents need re-indexing for the active
model" in amber. Nothing needs it — matching indexes on first use. Reworded, and
no longer styled as a warning, with a separate line for when auto-indexing is on.

**Auto-index, opt in.** New `autoIndexOnUpload` preference. One hook mounted at
the root covers all three moments that create stale documents, because they all
surface identically as a non-zero `documents.stale`: a fresh import, an embedding
provider/model change, and leftovers from a previous session.

Backed by a NEW command rather than the existing one: `ai_reembed_all` re-embeds
every document unconditionally, so reusing it would re-bill a cloud embedding
provider for already-indexed documents each time a single file is added.
`ai_index_stale_documents` embeds only what is missing and returns a null job id
when nothing is. Both share one job body so they cannot drift in error handling,
cancellation or progress.

**Ask during setup.** New onboarding step immediately before the crash-reporting
consent — both ask "may this run on your behalf", and this one calls a provider
that may bill per token, so the two spend/privacy decisions sit together.

Defaults to OFF, and the step's switch is seeded from the stored value rather
than forced on: an existing install must never start calling a paid embedding
provider because of an update, and stepping back through the wizard must not
silently discard a "no". Leaving it off costs nothing — matching still indexes
lazily, which is the whole point of the first part.

* fix: auto-index a second upload that leaves the same stale count

The AI review found a HIGH in the guard I wrote, and it was right: the dedup key
was `provider/model/staleCount` and never reset. Import one résumé (stale 1,
indexed), import another (stale 1 again) and the second matched the previous key
and was skipped — auto-indexing silently died after the very first document. A
count identifies a situation, not a batch.

Two things were needed, and each protects against the other's failure mode.

Hold the concurrency guard until the JOB ends, not until indexStaleDocuments
resolves. That returns as soon as the job is spawned, so the status refetch
straight after it still reports the pre-run count and would start a second,
separately-billed run over the same documents. Now released on the job's
terminal event, via the same useJobEvents path the manual re-index already uses.

Keep a per-(space, count) attempt key, but CLEAR it once the index goes clean or
the space changes. Without the key, a run that fails to reduce the count
re-triggers the instant it ends — an unbounded loop of paid provider calls.
Without the reset, the reported bug.

The guard also had to become state rather than a ref: the effect must re-run
when a job finishes, and clearing a ref re-renders nothing.

Both halves are pinned, and the regression test was verified to fail against the
original guard rather than assumed to: removing the reset reproduces exactly the
reported symptom.

* fix: never run two embedding jobs at once, and stop the strip guessing

with no knowledge of each other, so a background auto-index and a button press
